top_five.text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing a severe Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus strain, with 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths recorded amid ongoing insecurity and responder evacuations.
An Israeli military strike on an MSF-operated clinic in Gaza killed two watchmen, highlighting severe protection risks facing humanitarian personnel and healthcare facilities.
A joint UN early warning report warned of expanding acute hunger across 16 global hotspots, designating Afghanistan as a country of very high concern and citing worsening food insecurity in Myanmar.
Ukraine submitted a Black Sea ceasefire proposal to safeguard critical maritime grain corridors following Russian strikes on two foreign grain carriers near Odesa.
A drone attack on a military facility in Kuwait killed two Italian nationals, elevating regional tensions after Italy stated the unmanned aircraft was produced in Iran.

top_story.quote: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is confronting an escalating Ebola outbreak marked by 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths, while active conflict, displacement, and low contact tracing severely impede containment operations.
top_story.label: AFRICA — Severe Ebola Outbreak and Response Impediments in DRC

Middle East.headline: Gaza/OPT — Israeli Strike on MSF Clinic Kills Two Staff Members
Middle East.body: An Israeli military strike targeted a clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Gaza, killing two watchmen. The facility was actively managed by the international medical humanitarian organization when the attack occurred. The incident highlights ongoing severe protection risks facing health workers and humanitarian infrastructure operating within Gaza.

Middle East.headline: Kuwait/Iran — Fatal Drone Attack on Military Facility Triggers Regional Tensions
Middle East.body: A drone strike on a military facility in Kuwait killed two Italian nationals. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani stated that the drone involved was manufactured in Iran. Tehran has denied responsibility for the attack. In response, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for increased international pressure on Tehran, citing Gulf security as essential to broader regional stability. The escalation coincides with threats to maritime shipping and a modest rise in global oil prices.

Middle East.headline: Syria — Security Forces Targeted in Drone and Armed Attacks in South
Middle East.body: Armed attacks in southern Syria have left security personnel dead and injured across two separate incidents. In Suwayda province, four members of Syria's internal security forces were injured in a bomb-laden drone attack carried out by armed groups along the Rima Hazem axis. State media reported this as the second drone strike in the area in less than a week. In a separate incident, gunmen killed two Syrian soldiers in the Daraa countryside.

Middle East.headline: Iran — Rights Group Warns of Severe Judicial Crackdown and Sentences
Middle East.body: Human rights advocates from Amnesty International report a severe deterioration in Iran's judicial process following the January 2026 protests. Demonstrators face death sentences and extrajudicial killings after trials described as grossly unfair and marred by torture. Authorities have reportedly sought to equate peaceful dissent with treason and espionage. Rights researchers are calling for an international criminal justice mechanism, such as a special tribunal, to ensure accountability for alleged crimes against humanity.

Americas.headline: Central America — UN warns of rising hunger as global hotspots expand
Americas.body: The Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme warned that severe hunger is set to worsen across 16 global hotspots over the next six months. Driven by conflict, displacement, economic distress, and extreme weather, the number of identified hotspots rose from 13 in June, with Central America, Chad, Uganda, and parts of southern Africa newly added to the watch list. Meanwhile, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria, and Yemen face the highest risk of famine.

Americas.headline: United States — Severe nor'easter causes coastal flooding and power outages
Americas.body: A powerful nor'easter coastal storm drenched the eastern United States, bringing heavy rain, high winds, and damaging coastal flooding from the Carolinas to New England. The storm rapidly intensified along the Atlantic seaboard, downing power lines and cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of customers. The severe weather disrupted air, rail, and road transit during peak Thanksgiving holiday travel.

Americas.headline: Canada — Immigration and travel restrictions extended over Ebola outbreak
Americas.body: The Government of Canada has extended temporary travel and border restrictions for an additional 90 days, maintaining the measures until 25 February 2027. Under the extended policy, immigration documents, visas, permits, and electronic travel authorizations remain suspended for foreign nationals residing in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan. Canadian authorities cited precautionary measures to prevent Ebola transmission into the country as monitoring of regional outbreaks continues.

Africa.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Escalating Ebola Outbreak and Insecurity
Africa.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is confronting a major Ebola outbreak, with official data recording 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths, representing a 49.1 percent fatality rate. Driven by the Bundibugyo virus strain—for which no approved vaccine or specific treatment exists—containment efforts are severely hampered by conflict, mass displacement, and low contact tracing. Recent heavy fighting trapped World Health Organization and national health responders in Akwe before their evacuation to Bunia. Additionally, analysis of cemetery records in Mongbwalu indicates that unregistered deaths may mean the actual casualty count is substantially higher, while a UNICEF survey reveals nearly six in 10 women and girls in the epicenter report worsening abuse.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Black Sea Ceasefire Offered Following Attacks on Foreign Grain Carriers
Europe.body: Ukraine has submitted a Black Sea ceasefire proposal to international partners to enable food exports, while awaiting a formal response from Moscow. The initiative follows Russian strikes targeting two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa. The proposal seeks to secure critical maritime corridors essential for global food security amid ongoing attacks on commercial shipping infrastructure.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian Drone Strike Injures Civilians and Damages Schools in Kremenchuk
Europe.body: A Russian unmanned aerial vehicle struck Kremenchuk in Ukraine's Poltava region on November 27, injuring four people, including three children. The strike inflicted extensive damage on two educational institutions in the city. Local authorities reported that all affected individuals are receiving necessary medical treatment.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Over $18 Million Secured for International Humanitarian Food Program
Europe.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that over $18 million has been raised to support the Grain from Ukraine humanitarian food program. Supported by financial contributions from Sweden, Norway, Finland, Japan, and Germany, the initiative facilitates the supply of Ukrainian food commodities to nations facing critical food insecurity.
verified_figures: Over $18 million secured for humanitarian food program

Asia-Pacific.headline: Asia-Pacific — UN Warns Worsening Hunger in Afghanistan and Myanmar
Asia-Pacific.body: A joint early warning report by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme warns that acute food insecurity will worsen across 16 global hotspots over the next six months. Driven primarily by armed conflict, economic instability, and climate shocks including the El Niño phenomenon, hunger risks are escalating worldwide. Within the Asia-Pacific region, Afghanistan has been designated as a country of very high concern, while Myanmar is also listed among the severely impacted nations facing heightened hunger threats from December through May 2027.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Nigeria — Health authorities activate emergency center following FCT cholera fatalities
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Federal Capital Territory Administration in Nigeria activated its Multisectoral Cholera Emergency Operations Centre to contain an ongoing outbreak across the territory. The response follows recent cholera deaths, including at least five recorded fatalities in the Gwagwa community within the Abuja Municipal Area Council. Health officials had previously warned that transmission in the country peaks between late August and October, with seasonal rainfall and flooding amplifying risks by contaminating public water sources.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Kenya — High Court orders suspension of US-backed Ebola quarantine facility
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Kenya's High Court ordered the suspension of construction and operations at a 50-bed US-backed Ebola quarantine facility located at Laikipia Air Base near Nanyuki. The court gave Kenyan authorities 45 days to comply with constitutional disclosure requirements regarding the agreement with Washington. The project was initially approved by President William Ruto following a request from US President Donald Trump. Prior to the suspension order, the facility had accommodated seven American aid workers who had been deployed to Ebola response efforts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

escalation_risks.potential_impact: Escalating hostilities risk causing civilian casualties, localized displacement, and restricted movement across southern Syria.
